channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: Digital home key and car key on your phone: how they work now
item.description: Your phone's wallet app can now hold keys for compatible front doors, cars and hotel rooms, and since 11 November Google Wallet holds home keys too, using Aliro, a smart lock standard backed by Apple, Google and Samsung.

item.title: MacBook Pro OLED vs mini-LED: what the $400 PROLED screen adds
item.description: Apple now sells the MacBook Pro with two kinds of screen: the mini-LED Liquid Retina XDR and the new tandem OLED PROLED XDR, which costs $400 more with the same chip and adds touch, deeper blacks and a lighter body.

item.title: Open source vs closed source password managers: what it means for you
item.description: An open source password manager lets anyone read its code, while a closed source one relies on audits by firms it hires; either way, your master password and two-factor sign-in decide most of how safe your vault is.

item.title: Gemini Google Wallet connection: spending charts, subscriptions, budgets
item.description: Gemini app users in the US can now connect Google Wallet so Gemini can chart their spending, spot subscriptions that went up in price and suggest a budget. The connection is off until you turn it on, and Gemini can only read the data.

item.title: E-ZPass scam text on iPhone and Android: how to spot it and what to do
item.description: Texts that claim you owe an unpaid E-ZPass toll and push you to pay through a link are a known scam, and US officials say not to tap the link. E-ZPass in New York says it never asks for card numbers or other personal details by text or email.

item.title: Alexa for Shopping on Amazon now in the UK and 13 more countries
item.description: Amazon's AI shopping assistant, Alexa for Shopping, now works in full in 14 countries, among them the UK, Canada, India, Germany and Australia, after starting in the US in May. It's free for anyone signed in to Amazon, with no Echo, Alexa app or Prime needed.

item.title: Apple Home doorbell and cameras from LG: prices and order date
item.description: The first Apple Home Collection accessories, made by LG, went on order on 13 November: an Indoor Cam for $199.95, a Video Doorbell for $249.95 and an Outdoor Cam for $299.95. They're expected to arrive in mid-December.

item.title: Apple TV 4K 2026 price: $299 model with hands-free Siri in stores now
item.description: Apple's fourth-generation Apple TV 4K costs $299 and reaches stores on November 13, with three microphones so you can talk to Siri without the remote. It comes in one version only: 128 GB with Wi-Fi and gigabit Ethernet.

item.title: Bobara is a calm capybara app that logs the boba teas you buy
item.description: Bobara ($4.99) shows Momo, a capybara soaking in a hot spring, and each boba tea you check in can bring him a new friend or treat. It was #89 among paid Entertainment apps on the US App Store on November 13.

item.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents buy things for you after you approve
item.description: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on 13 November, a payment feature that lets its Dots agents shop for you: you save a card once, and you approve every purchase with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint. It starts with ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US who are over 18.

item.title: Claude down on November 13: login errors on claude.ai and Claude Code
item.description: Claude had two separate problems on 13 November: first many people couldn't sign in to claude.ai, Claude Code and Claude Cowork, then claude.ai, the mobile apps, the API and Claude Code showed errors for about two and a half hours. Anthropic says both are fixed.

item.title: Clipzy AI video maker turns a typed idea into TikTok and Reels videos
item.description: Clipzy, a new web tool, writes a script from your idea, adds an AI voiceover, footage, captions and music, and hands you a vertical video for TikTok, Reels or Shorts. New users get 50 free credits without a card; paid plans start at $22 a month.

item.title: Desky switches Safari to desktop mode when you unfold the iPhone Duo
item.description: Desky is a $1.99 Safari extension for the iPhone Duo that loads the desktop version of a site when you open the phone and the mobile version when you fold it. It was #6 among paid Utilities apps on the US App Store on November 13.

item.title: Drunk Proof app locks your iPhone on a night out
item.description: Drunk Proof is a new iPhone app that locks everything except the apps you chose while sober, so you can't text an ex or email your boss after a few drinks. It was #99 in Lifestyle on the US App Store's paid chart on 13 November.

item.title: Euro-Office desktop app: free Office alternative for Windows, Mac, Linux
item.description: Nextcloud released the Nextcloud Office Desktop app, powered by Euro-Office, a free and open-source office suite for documents, spreadsheets, presentations and PDFs. It's out now for Windows, Linux and Apple Silicon Macs, and it edits files on your computer without an internet connection.

item.title: Fituous calorie tracker app keeps food, water and fasting in one place
item.description: Fituous is a new calorie and nutrition tracker for iPhone and iPad that puts your food diary, macros, water, fasting and weight in one view and works local-first. It was #47 in Health & Fitness on the US App Store's paid chart on 13 November.

item.title: GiggleCam camera app gets kids to look at the lens, made for iPhone Duo
item.description: GiggleCam is a new camera app that plays a silly animation next to the lens, like a dancing cheese shouting "Say cheese!", so children look at the camera. It was #56 in Photo & Video on the US App Store's paid chart on 13 November.

item.title: iPhone 18 delay may be tied to Samsung camera sensors, report says
item.description: Japan's Semicon Portal reports that Apple may be waiting for Samsung's Texas factory to make enough camera sensors for the standard iPhone 18, which didn't launch with the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. Apple hasn't explained the delay.

item.title: iPhone 18 release date: spring 2027 with A20 chip, Gurman says
item.description: The iPhone 18 and the cheaper iPhone 18e will come out in spring 2027 with Apple's A20 chip, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman; Apple hasn't announced either phone. He says the iPhone Air 2 is expected at the same time.

item.title: LAB Cam Pro: film camera app for RAW photos on iPhone and Mac
item.description: LAB Cam Pro is a new $4.99 camera and darkroom app that gives RAW photos the look of a chosen film stock, with grain and glow, and keeps the original. It was #51 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on November 13.

item.title: Lil Booth photo booth app for iPhone makes four-shot strips
item.description: Lil Booth is a 99-cent photo booth app for iPhone: pick a look and a frame, take four photos on a 3-2-1 countdown and save the finished strip to Photos. It was #39 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 13 November.

item.title: Lunda budget calendar app shows your balance for every day ahead
item.description: Lunda is a new budget calendar: you put bills, paydays and payments on the days they happen, and each day shows the balance it leaves you, weeks and months ahead. The calendar is free; forecasts and planners cost 69 dollars a year.

item.title: MONS peak finder app names the mountains you see, even offline
item.description: MONS is a 2.99-dollar peak finder app for iPhone that labels the summits in your camera view, from more than a million peaks worldwide, and works offline once you download an area. It was #63 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 13 November.

item.title: MyLilMatrix: Eisenhower matrix app for iPhone, one purchase
item.description: MyLilMatrix is a to-do app for iPhone and iPad that sorts your tasks into four boxes by how important and how urgent they are. It costs 99 cents once, with no subscription, and was #79 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 13 November.

item.title: Pretend Piano app turns your Apple Watch into an air guitar and piano
item.description: Pretend Piano: Air Instruments is a 99-cent Apple Watch app that turns wrist movements into music: strum for guitar, move your wrist side to side for violin, or tap a tabletop for piano. It was #16 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 13 November, five days after it came out.

item.title: Setomi lifting log app turns your PDF or photo plan into a workout log
item.description: Setomi reads a lifting plan you already have, from a PDF, a spreadsheet, a photo or a note, and lets you log it set by set on iPhone and Apple Watch. It costs $1.99 once, with no subscription and no account.

item.title: Share mouse and keyboard between Mac and Windows with free ZeroG
item.description: ZeroG is a new free, open-source app from ReggieSoft that lets one mouse and keyboard control several computers on the same network: move the cursor past the edge of one screen and it jumps to the next.

item.title: Siri AI on Apple TV 4K 2nd and 3rd gen: tvOS 27.2.1 is out
item.description: Apple released tvOS 27.2.1 on November 13, and it brings Siri AI to the 2nd- and 3rd-generation Apple TV 4K. It only works with a paired Siri AI-capable iPhone or iPad nearby, such as an iPhone 15 Pro or later.

item.title: Snow day predictor app Snow Day Radar shows your school district's odds
item.description: Snow Day Radar gives the chance of a snow day, delay or virtual day for every public school district in the lower 48 US states, with the reason in plain words. The free app came out on 11 November and was #2 among free Weather apps on the US App Store on 13 November.

item.title: ToneBird AI reply assistant drafts replies in Gmail, Slack and WhatsApp
item.description: ToneBird is a Mac and Windows app that writes reply drafts in your own tone inside apps like Gmail, Slack, WhatsApp and iMessage, using what it knows about each person. You still press send yourself.

item.title: Uber data breach: driver's license data of thousands of drivers stolen
item.description: Hackers took personal and driver's license information of thousands of US Uber drivers through Fireworks AI, an outside AI company Uber worked with. Uber is sending notices and offering free credit monitoring.

item.title: Vellumi cruise journal app keeps your ports, photos and notes offline
item.description: Vellumi is a $3.99 iPhone and iPad app for keeping a private diary of a cruise: plan the ports and sea days, then add photos, videos, voice notes, meals and shows to each day. It was #61 in Travel on the US App Store's paid chart on 13 November.

item.title: YouTube not working on new Apple TV 4K: how to fix the error
item.description: Some owners of the new Apple TV 4K that started shipping on 13 November see the message 'YouTube is not yet available on this device' when they open YouTube. 9to5Mac and MacRumors report a fix: update to tvOS 27.2, restart, then reinstall the app.

item.title: YouTube TV 'Video unavailable' error interrupts shows and live sports
item.description: YouTube TV viewers report a black 'Video unavailable' screen that cuts into shows and games for about 10 seconds, sometimes several times in one broadcast. Google hasn't commented yet.

item.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: a faster Gemini 4 model for everyone in the Gemini app
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster model for everyday tasks and coding, and it's available to everyone in the Gemini app and Google Search, not just paying subscribers.

item.title: Microsoft 365 outage on 12 November hit Outlook, Teams and OneDrive
item.description: Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services went down for many users on 12 November. Microsoft confirmed the problem could affect connectivity for users in any region.

item.title: Why apps now charge for AI: credits, usage packs and premium plans
item.description: AI features cost companies money every time you use them, so apps are moving from "free AI" to limits, credits and paid tiers, and this month brought several examples.

item.title: Google and Samsung AI glasses with Gemini go on pre-order from $395
item.description: Google and Samsung's Intelligent Eyewear smart glasses, with Gemini built in, are on pre-order in frames from Warby Parker starting at $395 and from Gentle Monster starting at $449.

item.title: iPhone Duo after the first weeks: problems, settings and apps to know
item.description: Apple's first foldable iPhone has drawn complaints about cracking inner screens, Touch ID and settings you can only pick once, while a wave of small apps now uses its fold.

item.title: Scams going around this week: fake upgrades, fake invites, fake bills
item.description: This week's scams all copy a company you trust, a phone network, OpenAI or your internet provider, and push you to act fast; checking through the company's own app stops most of them.

item.title: AndroSnitch: old Chrome versions let hackers into Android phones
item.description: Security firm Sekoia warns of AndroSnitch, malware that infects Android phones with Qualcomm chips through fake websites, using flaws in old Chrome versions and a graphics driver. Both are fixed in updates.

item.title: Affinity for iPad is out: Canva's free design app with Apple Pencil
item.description: Canva launched Affinity for iPad, combining sketching, vector design, photo editing and page layout in one app with Apple Pencil support. The core tools are free for individuals.

item.title: Opera One on iPhone adds Data Saver, cutting data use up to 80%
item.description: Opera's browser for iPhone now has Data Saver, which compresses images and text on Opera's servers before they reach your phone; Opera says it can cut data use by up to 80%.

item.title: Actually Up is an alarm that only stops once you're out of bed
item.description: Actually Up's alarm pauses for two minutes when you press Stop and ends only when you stand up; your Apple Watch can count 20 steps to prove it. It was #35 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 12 November.

item.title: Glucose Relay copies FreeStyle Libre readings into Apple Health
item.description: In many countries LibreLink doesn't save glucose readings to Apple Health; Glucose Relay copies your FreeStyle Libre readings there automatically. It was #71 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 12 November.

item.title: PulseO2 brings blood oxygen readings back to your Apple Watch face
item.description: In the US, Apple Watch blood oxygen results only show in the Health app on iPhone; PulseO2 puts each new reading back on your watch face and in its app. It was #72 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 12 November.

item.title: YouTube Premium account sharing services cut off: Seoul warns buyers
item.description: Seoul's city government has warned again about cheap YouTube Premium account-sharing services, after 2,323 complaints this year from buyers who paid upfront and lost access early. Most of them, 1,728, came in October alone.

item.title: APCOA Flow parking app: pay for parking and EV charging by phone
item.description: APCOA Flow, a free app from car park operator APCOA, lets you find a car park, pay by phone and extend your parking without going back to the car. It was #58 in the UK App Store's top free apps on 12 November.

item.title: Apple HomeView review and price: $299 smart display out November 13
item.description: Apple's HomeView, a 7-inch smart display and home hub run by Siri, goes on sale on November 13 for $299, and the first reviews are out. Engadget gives it 8.4 out of 10 but says it leans on an iPhone or iPad and isn't built for watching video.

item.title: Brave removes Meta's hidden ID from Facebook and Instagram photos
item.description: Brave's desktop browser now deletes a hidden marker that Meta puts inside Facebook and Instagram photos when you save or upload one. The marker can make it easier to match the same picture across accounts and sites.
